title: Mailchimp vs Brevo vs Kit: Which Email Marketing Platform Fits a Small Business in 2026?
excerpt: Compare Mailchimp, Brevo and Kit by pricing model, free limits, automation and audience fit. Choose an email platform without paying for features your business will not use.
html:
Mailchimp, Brevo and Kit can all send newsletters, but they are built for different business models. Mailchimp is a broad marketing suite with contact-based plan limits. Brevo combines email with CRM and other channels, and its pricing is structured around sending volume and contact storage. Kit is designed for creators who build an audience through newsletters, forms and digital products.

The best choice depends on how your list grows, how often you email it and whether you need automated customer journeys. A platform that is inexpensive for a newsletter creator may be a poor fit for an ecommerce team that needs purchase-triggered campaigns and multiple staff accounts.

Pricing note: This comparison uses public US-dollar pricing and vendor help pages checked on November 8, 2026. Prices are starting points, not quotes for every list size. Currency, tax, billing term, location, add-ons and contact or send tier can change the amount you pay.

Quick verdict

  • Mailchimp: Start here if you want a broad marketing suite, a large integration ecosystem and familiar campaign and reporting tools.
  • Brevo: Start here if you store a sizeable contact database but send selectively, or want email alongside sales and multichannel tools.
  • Kit: Start here if your business is built around a newsletter, creator audience, digital products or paid subscriptions.

There is no universal winner. Compare the plan tier that covers your actual list, send volume, automation and team needs—not just the lowest number on a pricing page.

Mailchimp vs Brevo vs Kit: at a glance

PlatformFree-plan headlinePublished paid starting pointMain pricing driverBest fit
Mailchimp250 contacts; 500 sends per month, capped at 250 per dayEssentials from $13/month; Standard from $20/monthContact tier and monthly send allowanceSmall businesses wanting a broad marketing suite
Brevo300 sends per day; up to 100,000 stored contacts; limited automationStarter from $9/month; Standard from $18/monthMonthly send volume plus contact-storage tierBusinesses balancing list size and sending volume
KitUp to 10,000 active subscribers and unlimited broadcastsCreator from $39/month; Pro from $79/month at the 1,000-subscriber tierActive subscriber count and plan levelNewsletter writers and digital-product creators

These are vendor-advertised starting points, not like-for-like quotes. Mailchimp's paid plans use contact tiers and monthly send multipliers: its pricing page lists 10 times the contact count for Essentials, 12 times for Standard and 15 times for Premium. Brevo pairs monthly send volume with contact storage. Kit prices by active subscribers and plan features.

1. Mailchimp: best for a broad marketing toolkit

Mailchimp is worth considering when email is one part of a wider marketing operation. It combines campaigns, audience management, forms, reporting and a large integration catalogue. That can help a retailer, service business or marketing team connect ecommerce, analytics and customer systems without assembling every part separately.

Strengths: a broad set of integrations, established campaign tools, paid-plan scheduling and testing, and more advanced automation on higher tiers. Standard adds more optimisation and automation capability than Essentials.

Trade-offs: the free plan is now a small testing tier, not a long-term option for a growing list. It is limited to 250 contacts and 500 monthly sends. Because paid pricing is contact-based, your bill can rise as your database grows even if you do not increase campaign frequency. Check how the vendor counts contacts, what happens at the send limit and whether overage charges apply.

Choose Mailchimp when its integrations and marketing features save enough operational work to justify the contact-tier cost. Before subscribing, enter your expected contact count and send volume in its pricing calculator.

2. Brevo: best when sending volume matters more than stored contacts

Brevo's pricing structure can suit a business that keeps a large customer database but sends campaigns to selected segments. Its Free plan allows up to 100,000 stored contacts, while daily sending is capped at 300 emails. That storage allowance does not mean every contact can be emailed without consent or that every automation feature is free.

Strengths: volume-based tiers, free sales features and options to add channels such as SMS or WhatsApp where available. Brevo's published entry tiers pair 5,000 sends with up to 500 contacts, 10,000 sends with up to 1,500, and 15,000 sends with up to 2,500.

Trade-offs: the free daily cap can constrain a large campaign. Automation is limited to 2,000 contacts on Free; Standard adds marketing automation for unlimited contacts, A/B testing and advanced reporting. Multichannel add-ons may have separate credits, eligibility and charges.

Choose Brevo when your sending pattern fits its volume tiers and you want more than a newsletter tool. Calculate both stored contacts and total monthly sends, including triggered messages, before selecting a plan.

3. Kit: best for newsletter-led businesses and creators

Kit is designed around creators who publish regularly, collect subscribers through forms and landing pages, and earn from products or memberships. Its free Newsletter plan supports up to 10,000 active subscribers and unlimited broadcasts, which is attractive if you mainly send newsletters.

Strengths: creator-focused forms, landing pages, tagging and segmentation, plus tools for digital products and recurring subscriptions. Paid Creator adds visual automations and email sequences; Pro adds deeper analytics, collaboration and deliverability reporting.

Trade-offs: the free plan does not include visual automations or email sequences. If your business relies on multi-step onboarding, lead nurturing or post-purchase education, budget for a paid tier from the start. Kit's help centre lists Creator at $39 per month and Pro at $79 per month for up to 1,000 subscribers; annual billing is advertised as two months free. Prices scale with subscriber count, so check the renewal amount and tier.

Choose Kit when your newsletter is a product or a core audience channel. If you need a full sales CRM or complex ecommerce journeys, compare a broader platform as well.

How to estimate the real cost

Use the unit each vendor charges for:

  • Mailchimp: model your highest expected contact tier and its send multiplier. It is straightforward when the list is stable, but can cost more as stored contacts grow.
  • Brevo: model monthly sends and contact storage together. It can be attractive when you store many contacts but send selectively.
  • Kit: model active subscribers, then decide whether broadcasts alone are enough or whether you need paid automations and sequences.

For example, a creator with 4,000 active readers who sends one newsletter each week may be able to use Kit Free while staying below its subscriber limit and avoiding paid automation features. A retailer with 4,000 customer records but only occasional segmented campaigns should compare Brevo's volume tiers. A business that relies on a broad ecommerce integration stack may prefer Mailchimp even if its contact-based plan costs more.

These are workflow examples, not price quotes. Add staff seats, taxes, add-ons, triggered messages, annual renewal and migration effort to your budget. Check how each vendor treats inactive, unsubscribed or duplicate records before importing a list.

Choose by workflow, not feature count

If email needs to connect to a CRM, compare the whole customer workflow. Our HubSpot vs Pipedrive vs Zoho CRM comparison explains how sales seats and CRM pricing affect the decision. If you want to connect signups, sales updates and reporting, see our Zapier vs Make automation-cost guide. For a wider small-business software stack, read our practical AI tools guide.

Deliverability: do these steps before your first campaign

No platform can guarantee that every message reaches the inbox. Sender reputation, authentication, list quality, recipient engagement and message content all matter. A polished template cannot compensate for an old list or missing domain authentication.

  1. Authenticate your sending domain. Follow the vendor's current instructions for SPF and DKIM, and publish a DMARC policy that fits your mail setup. Do not copy DNS records from an unrelated domain.
  2. Import only eligible contacts. Keep the source, date and method of consent. A purchased, scraped or publicly visible address is not automatically eligible for marketing.
  3. Start with a relevant segment. Send to recent, engaged subscribers first and suppress hard bounces and unsubscribed contacts.
  4. Test the complete journey. Check the signup form, welcome message, links, mobile rendering and unsubscribe flow before launching.
  5. Measure useful outcomes. Track clicks, replies, purchases, qualified leads and unsubscribes. Treat open rates carefully because privacy features can distort tracking.
  6. Keep an export plan. Know how to export contacts, consent records, segments, templates and automation logic before you depend on a platform.

Consent rules for US, UK, Canadian and Australian audiences

Email rules depend on the sender, recipient and message type. A platform's compliance features do not make a campaign automatically lawful. This is a practical orientation, not legal advice; check the rules that apply to your business.

  • United States: The FTC's CAN-SPAM guidance requires accurate sender information, non-deceptive subject lines, a valid physical postal address and a clear opt-out. Opt-out requests must be honoured within 10 business days. The rules also cover commercial business-to-business email.
  • Canada: CASL generally requires prior express or qualifying implied consent, sender identification and contact information, and a working unsubscribe mechanism. The CRTC says unsubscribe requests must be processed within 10 business days. Keep evidence of the consent basis.
  • United Kingdom: Under PECR, unsolicited marketing email to individual subscribers generally needs consent unless a specific soft opt-in applies. Different rules can apply to corporate subscribers. Do not hide the sender's identity and provide a valid contact address for opt-outs.
  • Australia: The ACMA says commercial messages need consent, must identify the sender and include contact details, and must make unsubscribing easy. The Spam Act requires unsubscribe requests to be actioned within five working days.

Use consent fields, suppression lists and unsubscribe tools, but keep your own records of when and how each person subscribed. Do not upload a list simply because the software accepts the file.

A seven-step buying checklist

  1. Record your current marketable contacts and expected growth over the next year.
  2. Estimate campaign sends plus triggered emails such as welcome and post-purchase messages.
  3. List the automations you actually need: welcome, lead follow-up, customer education or re-engagement.
  4. Confirm how many staff need access and whether approvals are required.
  5. Check integrations with your website, CRM, ecommerce platform and analytics tools.
  6. Compare the total cost at your expected contact and send tier, including taxes, add-ons and renewal.
  7. Run a small pilot, test consent and unsubscribe handling, and export a backup before migrating the full list.

Frequently asked questions

Which platform is cheapest?

There is no single cheapest option for every business. Kit has a free plan for up to 10,000 active subscribers if broadcasts are enough. Brevo has a 300-per-day free send cap and large contact storage. Mailchimp's free plan is limited to 250 contacts and 500 monthly sends. Paid costs depend on the list, send volume and features required.

Is Brevo better than Mailchimp for a small business?

Brevo can fit better when you store many contacts but send fewer campaigns, or when its sales and multichannel tools match your workflow. Mailchimp can fit better when its integration ecosystem and broader marketing tools save time. Compare the same list size, monthly sends and automation needs in both calculators.

Is Kit suitable for a service business?

It can work if the main job is publishing a newsletter, collecting subscribers and selling services or digital products to an audience. If you need a sales pipeline, support workflows or complex ecommerce segmentation, compare a broader CRM or marketing platform.

Will changing platforms improve inbox placement?

Not automatically. Authentication, sender reputation, list quality, consent, bounce handling and recipient engagement still matter. A new platform can provide better tools, but it cannot guarantee inbox placement.

The bottom line

Mailchimp is the broad marketing-suite option, Brevo is worth a close look when send volume and contact storage drive the economics, and Kit is built for creators who make a newsletter part of their business. Start with your audience model and required workflows, then compare the real plan tier—not the lowest advertised price.

Pricing and features change. Recheck the linked vendor pages before signing up, especially for annual offers, country-specific billing and add-ons.
